problem_statement: When the shell is built with the shell_builtin_cmd_help_json module, the shell must provide a help_json command. Invoking help_json must print a single-line machine-readable JSON object describing the commands available to the shell. The JSON object must have a top-level "cmds" array. Each element of that array must be an object with string fields "cmd" and "desc", containing the command name and its description. The output must include every command that the shell can run.

verification.reason: The core behaviour is specified, but the hidden tests additionally require the module to be buildable, the listed set to be exact and duplicate-free, built-in help/help_json to be excluded, and XFA-registered commands to be included. These can be added without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden test enables USEMODULE += shell_builtin_cmd_help_json, so the build system must recognize that module, but the statement does not state that the module itself must be made available to the build system.

The tests require each available command to appear exactly once and use the registered command name and description; the statement does not explicitly rule out duplicates or clarify that names/descriptions must match the registered commands.
The statement says the output must include every command the shell can run, but the tests exclude the built-in help and help_json commands themselves, which could reasonably be read as included.

The tests include commands registered through the shell's XFA command mechanism (e.g. periodic), while the statement only says every command and may not make it clear that all registration mechanisms must be included.

leak_check.leak_detail: The phrases 'commands registered in the normal shell command list' and 'commands registered through the shell's XFA command mechanism' hint at the internal command data sources used by the fix, but they do not give the JSON formatting or iteration algorithm.
leak_check.suggested_statement: When the shell is built with the shell_builtin_cmd_help_json module, the shell must provide a help_json command. Invoking help_json must print a single-line, valid JSON object, followed by a newline, describing the commands available to the shell. The JSON object must have a top-level "cmds" array. Each element of that array must be an object with string fields "cmd" and "desc", containing the command name and its description. The cmds array must contain every command that can be executed through the shell, including all commands registered with the shell, and each command must appear exactly once. The built-in help and help_json commands themselves must not be included in the array.
